result.reason: Section 20(d) reaches the preferred position: Sparkling may assign to affiliates and M&A successors without consent; Garman otherwise requires Sparkling’s consent, subject to a reasonableness standard, and may never assign to a Sparkling competitor; and Sparkling’s change of control creates no termination right. However, the revision to Section 3(c) is overbroad: the phrase “or as permitted under Section 20(d)” grammatically applies to transfers, leases, exports and sublicences of the Work, potentially permitting conduct unrelated to assignment. That undermines unrelated commercial intent and should instead preserve those restrictions while addressing only assignment of the Agreement. The additions concerning partial assignments, suspension and repricing also go beyond the stated preferred position.
